content.text: Our shop keeps carts in a 4 KB session cookie and long carts get cut short. Compare keeping carts in Redis or in Postgres in a short paragraph, recommend one, and leave the choice to me. Do not read or write any files.

Moving carts out of the cookie and into a server-side store fixes the 4 KB limit either way. Redis gives you fast reads and writes, and expiry comes built in via TTLs, which suits abandoned carts. Its weakness is durability: unless you configure persistence, a restart or eviction can lose carts, and if you don't already run Redis, it's a new system to operate. Postgres keeps carts durable, lets you query them for analytics or recovery emails, and needs no new infrastructure if you already run it. Its costs are slightly slower writes on every cart change and a scheduled job to purge stale carts. I'd recommend Postgres, since carts are business data that shouldn't disappear, and it adds no new system. Redis is the better fit only if carts are purely ephemeral and Redis is already in your stack.

input.title: Choose cart storage: Redis or Postgres
input.body:
Long carts overflow the 4 KB session cookie. Move carts to a server-side store keyed by a session ID in the cookie.

- **Postgres (recommended):** durable, queryable for analytics and recovery emails, no new infrastructure if already in use. Costs slightly slower cart writes and a purge job for stale carts.
- **Redis:** fast, TTL-based expiry built in. Carts can be lost on restart or eviction unless persistence is configured, and it adds a system to run if you don't already have one.

actions: a1 resolve "Use Postgres", a2 resolve "Use Redis"
